answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, externally costly resource—such as a token stake—and slash it when independent audits show fabricated work or collusive behavior. The rule does not prove a real-world identity; it makes multiplying identities expensive, while reputation and task access grow only from verified contributions. Like a lantern in a garden viewed through a prism, the stake makes hidden coordination easier to expose, but attackers still pay capital costs and risk losing every tainted account’s deposit.
